source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 145: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assumptions for variant 145: hold the model and tokenizer, precision, runtime build, hardware, serving configuration, autoscaling policy, and a versioned short/long request mix fixed; state units and label estimates versus measurements. Hypothesis: at the declared offered load, the candidate scheduling or admission change raises completed goodput by at least 5% versus baseline, without increasing queue-inclusive end-to-end P99 latency by more than 10% and without a correctness regression. Run a randomized paired crossover using the same seeded requests, counterbalanced baseline/candidate order, isolated background load, a declared warm-up discard, and independent repetitions until a prespecified confidence/precision target or safety stopping rule is met. Capture arrival, queue enter/exit, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, decode-step, completion, cancellation, timeout, and error timestamps per request. Define TTFT as arrival to first token and also publish service-only TTFT; define TPOT with an explicit generated-token denominator and say whether the first-token interval is excluded. Report request/s and token/s throughput, goodput numerator and denominator, queue-time distribution, prefill and decode rates, and queue-inclusive end-to-end P50/P95/P99 with workload-stratum denominators. Record prompt/input and output lengths, concurrency/offered load, batch composition, retries, cancellations, timeouts, errors, and correctness checks. Collect GPU utilization, memory high-water mark, KV-cache occupancy/evictions/OOMs, power, clocks, temperature, CPU, network, and scheduler telemetry with synchronized clocks. Analyze paired deltas and uncertainty by short/long and prefill/decode strata; treat warm-up, load drift, thermal throttling, batching, cache state, client effects, and failures as confounders. Require trace completeness, config provenance, reproducible seeds, and raw telemetry before attributing causality. Roll back or stop if correctness regresses, safety/error/timeout rates breach declared limits, OOMs or thermal limits occur, or the latency guardrail fails; otherwise report the hypothesis as supported only if its prespecified intervals and thresholds pass. Results are provisional and require domain-expert review.
risks: The hypothesis thresholds and workload mix are evaluation choices, not universal guarantees; conclusions are limited to the declared model, runtime, hardware, load, and strata.
Missing or unsynchronized request traces, cache-state drift, batching, retries, thermal throttling, client overhead, and correlated paired trials can bias latency or goodput comparisons.
evidence_required: Versioned model/runtime/hardware, serving, autoscaling, scheduler, tokenizer, precision, workload, seed, and offered-load configuration.
Complete synchronized request lifecycle traces, correctness/error records, repeated paired trial results with uncertainty, and GPU/KV/CPU/power/thermal telemetry.
